teaching.hint: If accepted events never overlap and are ordered by start time, which ones could overlap a new interval?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: In a sorted set of disjoint intervals, only the nearest predecessor and nearest successor by start can overlap a new interval.
solution_outline.approach: Maintain accepted bookings ordered by start. For each proposal, compare it with the first booking starting at or after its start and with the immediately previous booking; insert only if neither intersects it.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: All stored bookings are pairwise disjoint and ordered. The immediate predecessor has the latest end among prior starts, and the successor has the earliest start among later starts.
solution_outline.correctness: Any earlier booking ends no later than the predecessor, and any later booking starts no earlier than the successor. Passing those two overlap tests therefore rules out all conflicts; inserting preserves the invariant.
solution_outline.complexity: O(log B) time per booking with an ordered set and O(B) total space for B accepted bookings.
solution_outline.pitfall: Treating touching endpoints as an overlap rejects valid half-open neighboring events.

common_wrong_turns: Check only one side of the insertion point
source_fidelity_notes: Retained transactional rejection behavior and half-open boundary example.
